acupoints.notes: This is a strengthening point. For anaemia, dizziness, blurred vision and excessive fatigue, needle for ten minutes, withdraw, and then apply three to five moxa cones, moxaing every other day for two months; this can extend life and promote health, working much as Zusanli does.

acupoints.code: III.P.3. Forearm, posterior – Shouwujin – Shouqianjin zone
acupoints.name: Shouwujin and Shouqianjin
acupoints.anatomy: Branch nerve of the liver, branch nerve of the lung.
acupoints.location: Shouwujin: locate with the hand resting on the chest, 6.5 cun above the transverse wrist crease — that is, 0.5 cun lateral and 0.5 cun above Huoshan. Shouqianjin: 8 cun above the transverse wrist crease and 4 cun below the transverse elbow crease — that is, 1.5 cun above Shouwujin.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver and Lung channels.
acupoints.properties: Courses the sinews and quickens the connecting vessels, clears the blood and resolves toxin.
acupoints.indications: Sciatica, numbness of the hands and feet, distension of the lower leg, foot pain, resolving excess cholesterol, resolving pain at the needle site, neck pain, headache, abdominal pain, drug poisoning, food poisoning, toxic sores and ulcers.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness and distension with slight numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: Shouwujin and Shouqianjin are among Tung's 72 principal needlings and are also key points among Tung's 32 resolving needlings, able to relieve numbness, distension and toxicity. Used together as a dao ma pair they work better still; they are seldom used singly.

acupoints.code: III.M.1. Forearm, medial – Sanmen zone
acupoints.name: Changmen
acupoints.anatomy: Changmen: the dorsal branch of the ulnar artery, the ulnar nerve, the branch nerve of the liver and the accessory renal nerve. Ganmen: extensor digitorum communis, branches given off from the interosseous artery of the forearm, and the branch nerve of the liver. Xinmen: within the biceps, the inferior ulnar collateral artery, branches of the radial nerve and the branch nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: Locate with the hand resting on the chest. Changmen: between the ulnar border of the ulna and the tendon, 3 cun from the crease at the pisiform. Ganmen: at the middle of the ulnar border of the ulna, 6 cun above the transverse wrist crease. Xinmen: in the depression on the ulnar side of the proximal ulna, 1.5 cun below the tip of the elbow.
acupoints.meridian: Changmen: enters the Gallbladder and Large Intestine channels. Ganmen: enters the Liver and Gallbladder channels. Xinmen: enters the Heart channel.
acupoints.properties: Changmen: courses and drains the intestinal bowels. Ganmen: courses the liver and rectifies qi. Xinmen: frees the connecting vessels of the heart.
acupoints.indications: Changmen: acute and chronic enteritis, dizziness and blurred vision, cholecystitis, vomiting, diarrhoea. Ganmen: acute hepatitis (specifically effective), acute and chronic gastroenteritis, chest oppression, chest pain, pain in both flanks, pain on the inner side of the leg. Xinmen: heart disease, heightened palpitations, chest oppression, vomiting, dry cholera.
acupoints.technique: Changmen: perpendicular insertion, 0.3–1 cun. Ganmen: perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun; liver pain resolves as soon as the needle is in — turning the needle to the right relieves chest oppression, turning it to the left also removes intestinal pain. Xinmen: perpendicular insertion, 0.5–0.8 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Changmen: soreness and distension reaching straight to the fingers. Xinmen: soreness and distension with slight numbness.
acupoints.application: Changmen is mostly paired with Ganmen as a dao ma to strengthen the effect.
acupoints.notes: In treating liver conditions the Upper Three Huang points are mostly used as the main points and Ganmen less often; Ganmen is also seldom used alone, being combined with Xinmen and Changmen as a dao ma, which frees the triple burner and regulates the whole body.

acupoints.code: III.A.9. Forearm, anterior – Sanshi zone
acupoints.name: Renshi
acupoints.anatomy: Renshi: the cutaneous nerve of the outer arm, the subcutaneous branch of the radial nerve, the nerve of the lung and the branch nerve of the heart. Dishi: branches of the median nerve, the branch nerve of the lung and the branch nerve of the heart. Tianshi: the radial nerve, the posterior brachial nerve and the median nerve, the branch nerve of the lung and the accessory renal nerve.
acupoints.location: Renshi: arm extended level, palm facing up, 3 cun above the transverse wrist crease, on the upper border of the radial side of the radius. Dishi: palm facing up, 6 cun above the transverse wrist crease on the upper border of the radial side of the radius — that is, 3 cun above Renshi. Tianshi: on the upper border of the radial side of the palmar aspect of the radius, 3 cun above Dishi; take it 3 cun below the crease of the cubital fossa.
acupoints.meridian: Renshi: enters the Heart, Lung and Kidney channels. Dishi: enters the Lung and Kidney channels. Tianshi: enters the Lung channel.
acupoints.properties: Courses the heart and rectifies qi, clears and diffuses lung qi.
acupoints.indications: Renshi: asthma, palm pain, finger pain, shoulder and arm pain, back pain, chest pain, palpitations, proteinuria. Dishi: asthma, common cold, headache, kidney depletion, lower back pain, heart disease, hernia, constipation. Tianshi: asthma, rhinitis, arm pain, common cold, chest pain, chest oppression, bronchitis.
acupoints.technique: Renshi: oblique insertion — along the upper border of the radial side of the palmar aspect of the radius, from lateral to medial at 15 degrees, 0.5–1.5 cun. Dishi: oblique insertion from lateral to medial at 15 degrees, 0.5–1.5 cun. Tianshi: oblique insertion, 1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Renshi and Tianshi: local soreness and distension. Dishi: local soreness and distension, sometimes spreading to the forearm.
acupoints.application: Needled to 0.5 cun it treats asthma, palm and finger pain, shoulder and arm pain, and back pain (for illness on the right use the left point, and for illness on the left the right). Needled to 1 cun it treats heart disease and palpitations (as recorded in Master Tung's book).
acupoints.notes: Master Tung's book gives Renshi as 4 cun above the crease, Master Hu's as 3 cun; clinical experience bears out the latter, and since Master Tung's book was never revised, Master Hu's figure is followed here. The point has three layers of depth: shallow insertion reaches the Lung channel, the middle layer enters the Heart channel, and the deep layer the Kidney channel. Needled 0.5–0.8 cun Renshi treats asthma; around 1–1.2 cun it treats palpitations and heart disease; at 1.5 cun it treats kidney depletion and proteinuria. In Tung's acupuncture the channel a point enters changes with the depth of insertion, and so do the conditions it treats — a defining feature of the system. Tianshi, Dishi and Renshi together are specifically effective for asthma.

acupoints.code: III.A.6. Forearm, anterior – Houling zone
acupoints.name: Houling
acupoints.anatomy: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm; branch nerve of the lung.
acupoints.location: 1.5 cun directly below Shaohai, then 0.5 cun toward the lateral side.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Lung channel.
acupoints.properties: Clears the lung and diffuses the orifices, transforms stasis and dissipates binds.
acupoints.indications: Rhinitis, blocked nose, laryngitis, tonsillitis, goitre, sore throat, nasal cancer.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.2–0.3 cun. Spot-pricking with a three-edged needle to release stagnant blood is specifically effective.
acupoints.notes: This point was not made public in Master Tung's original work; Master Hu set it out on the basis of what Master Tung taught day to day. For rhinitis and blocked nose, Tung's acupuncture mostly uses Jianli, Zhongli, Fenjin and Hejin, and may add Zhenjing, Shuijin, Shuitong, Shen'er and Sima, together with moxa at Jinyin and Jinyang and at the discoloured points over the heart and lung region of the back, and the Weimao qi points. But when a dark, discoloured mark appears over this point, it must be needled for the effect to be clear. For throat cancer and nasal cancer: besides this point, Waisanguan must be combined with it, and spot-pricking to bleed carried out around Sihua shang, Cesanli and Cexiasanli. For goitre: this point may be combined with Sanzhong, Sima and Xinling yi.

acupoints.code: III.P.2. Forearm, posterior – Houzhong zone
acupoints.name: Houzhong
acupoints.anatomy: Ulnar nerve; branch nerve of the lung; branch nerve of the kidney.
acupoints.location: On the back of the arm, 2.5 cun below the transverse elbow crease, 1 cun radial to Huofuhai; take it between the two tendons.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Lung channel.
acupoints.properties: Clears the lung and diffuses the orifices, transforms stasis and dissipates binds.
acupoints.indications: Throat cancer, laryngitis, tonsillitis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.application: Combined with Fenjin, Hejin and Neijin this point is specifically effective for cough, laryngitis, bronchitis and throat cancer.
acupoints.notes: This is Master Tung's accompanying point for throat cancer and works with remarkable speed, the effect showing the moment the needle goes in. Houzhong and Houling are both key points for throat cancer; Waisanguan may be added, along with retained needles at responsive points wherever they appear — keep to the rule of needling wherever a mark shows.

acupoints.code: III.A.4. Forearm, anterior – Ganling zone
acupoints.name: The Ganling points
acupoints.anatomy: Superficially, the medial and lateral cutaneous nerves of the forearm; deeply, the anterior interosseous artery and vein and the median nerve; the hepatic nerve and the renal nerve.
acupoints.location: As described above for Ganling.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver channel.
acupoints.properties: Courses the liver and rectifies qi.
acupoints.indications: Spinal periostitis, hepatitis, cirrhosis, liver pain, pain in both flanks, leukaemia (raised or lowered white cell count), splenomegaly, sciatica, hemiplegia, lower back ache, sinew and bone pain.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun; or oblique insertion from below upward, 2 cun.
acupoints.notes: Ganling yi, er and san work in the same way as the Upper Three Huang points. They are among Tung's 72 principal needlings and are specifically effective for liver disease. In practice the Upper Three Huang points are used as the main points for liver disease more often, unless a responsive or discoloured mark appears over Ganling, in which case it must be taken. Needles may be retained at the corresponding responsive point on the ear. There are three Ganling points, of which er is the principal one; for liver conditions they are always needled as a dao ma. Ganling does not appear in Master Tung's original work and was made public by Master Hu. For sinew and bone pain: Ganling with Santong, the Upper Three Huang points and the Lower Three Huang points.

acupoints.code: III.A.10. Forearm, anterior – Li zone
acupoints.name: Quling, Jianli and Zhongli
acupoints.anatomy: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm; deeply the radial nerve; the nerve of the heart and the branch nerve of the lung.
acupoints.location: Quling: palm facing up, 1.5 cun directly below the midpoint of the crease of the cubital fossa. Jianli is 0.5 cun lateral to Quling, and Zhongli 0.5 cun lateral to Jianli.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Lung channels.
acupoints.properties: Diffuses and guides lung qi, frees the connecting vessels of the heart.
acupoints.indications: Cramp, asthma, arthritis of the elbow, palpitations, goitre, cardiac enlargement, cardiac paralysis, chest pain, back pain, severe common cold, blocked nose, cough, asthma, bronchitis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun; or spot-pricked to bleed with a bloodletting needle.
acupoints.application: Needled shallowly this point treats the common cold, deeply it treats pneumonia. Spot-pricking with a bloodletting needle to release stagnant blood treats yang cholera and dry cholera, cardiac paralysis and pharyngitis, and relieves wheezing. For cough: Quling, Jianli, Zhongli, Huofuhai. For the common cold: Tianshi, Quling, Jianli, Zhongli, Shuijin, Shuitong.
acupoints.notes: Quling, Jianli and Zhongli together are specifically effective for the common cold, influenza and sinusitis.

acupoints.code: IV.A.2. Upper arm, anterior – Shoujin zone
acupoints.name: Fenjin, Hejin and Neijin
acupoints.anatomy: At the biceps brachii; the subcutaneous nerve of the upper arm and the distribution of the median nerve; the brachial artery, the cephalic vein, the branch nerve of the heart and the branch nerve of the lung.
acupoints.location: Fenjin: locate with the hand resting on the chest, at the centre of the lower part of the humerus, 1.5 cun from the crease of the cubital fossa. For the others see the individual point entries.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Lung channel.
acupoints.properties: Clears and depurates lung qi.
acupoints.indications: Specifically effective for the common cold, laryngitis, allergic rhinitis, sinusitis and cough.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun; dao ma needling may be used.
acupoints.notes: Hejin and Neijin do not appear in Master Tung's book and were made public by Master Hu. The three Jin points of the arm and the three anterior Shi points of the arm have similar functions; either group alone is enough.

acupoints.code: IV.E.1. Shoulder – Shoulder zone 1
acupoints.name: Jianzhong and Jianzhong (Jian-zhong and Jian-zhong)
acupoints.anatomy: At the lower border of the middle of the deltoid; the brachial artery, the cephalic vein and the branch nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: Jianzhong: with the arm hanging naturally at the side, 2.5 cun directly below the crease at the centre of the shoulder bone. Jianzhong (the second point) is 2 cun below it.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart channel.
acupoints.properties: Quickens the blood and dispels stasis, frees the channels and quickens the connecting vessels.
acupoints.indications: Arthritis of the knee, knee sprain, skin conditions (of the neck and of the arm), poliomyelitis, hemiplegia, heightened palpitations, shoulder pain, frozen shoulder, nosebleed, hardening of the vessels, scrofula, clearing the blood.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–2 cun. Jianzhong may be needled together with Jianzhong (the second point).

acupoints.code: IV.E.1. Shoulder – Shoulder zone 1
acupoints.name: Beimian
acupoints.anatomy: The deltoid, the circumflex humeral artery, branches of the cephalic vein, branches of the clavicular nerve and the dantian nerve.
acupoints.location: With the arm raised, 0.2 cun above the centre of the hollow at the joint seam of the shoulder bone.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Triple Burner channel.
acupoints.properties: Courses the liver and disinhibits the gallbladder, harmonises qi and blood.
acupoints.indications: Oppression in the abdomen, weakness of the voice.
acupoints.technique: Needle to a depth of 0.3–0.5 cun.
acupoints.application: Bloodletting with a bloodletting needle treats whole-body fatigue, aching in both legs, vomiting, liver cholera, yang cholera and yin-yang cholera.
acupoints.notes: Beimian lies close to Jianyu of the fourteen channels and the two seem to be located alike, but in fact they are about 0.2 cun apart. Jianyu of the fourteen channels is found with the arm raised level: outside the acromioclavicular joint there are two depressions, and the smaller anterior one is Jianyu, with Beimian 0.2 cun above it. Beimian and Jianyu differ in position, and their channel affiliation and indications are quite different — a distinction to be observed carefully. Master Tung told his students throughout his life that among all the points from the 1-1 to the 10-10 regions, none is identical to a point of the traditional fourteen channels; his followers should keep this firmly in mind. Some points in Master Tung's book are not set out clearly and are easily confused; anyone who penetrates to the essence of Tung's extraordinary points will see where their underlying principle lies.

acupoints.code: IV.A.3. Upper arm, anterior – Zong zone
acupoints.name: Renzong
acupoints.anatomy: Renzong: beside the biceps; the radial collateral artery, the cephalic vein and the medial cutaneous nerve of the arm, the accessory nerve of the lung, the branch nerve of the heart and the accessory nerve of the liver. Dizong: behind the cephalic vein; the circumflex humeral artery, the axillary nerve and the branch nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: Renzong: locate with the hand resting on the chest, 3.5 cun directly above the lateral end of the crease of the cubital fossa, close against the bone — that is, 3.5 cun above Quchi of the fourteen channels and 0.5 cun above Shouwuli. Dizong: 3 cun above Renzong, located with the hand resting on the chest.
acupoints.meridian: Renzong: enters the Lung, Stomach and Spleen channels. Dizong: enters the Heart channel.
acupoints.properties: Renzong: frees the channels and quickens the connecting vessels, regulates the spleen and stomach, diffuses the lung and disinhibits the throat. Dizong: returns yang and stems counterflow, opens the orifices and rouses the brain.
acupoints.indications: Renzong: arm pain, swollen painful feet, swollen painful elbow that will not move, jaundice, oedema of the four limbs, splenomegaly, gastritis and duodenitis, asthma, laryngitis, common cold. Dizong: can bring a yang-pattern patient back from the brink of death. It is the emergency point for cerebral haemorrhage, resolving the moment the needle goes in, and the emergency needling for cardiac paralysis and angina. It treats hemiplegia, heart disease, cardiac asthma, hepatic coma, numbness of the hands and feet, arteriosclerosis, chest and back pain, difficult breathing, cerebrovascular occlusion and similar conditions.
acupoints.technique: Renzong: perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun. At 0.5 cun it treats the common cold and asthma; at 0.8 cun, arm pain; at 1.2 cun, conditions of the liver, gallbladder and spleen. Dizong: perpendicular insertion, 1–2 cun. At 1 cun for mild conditions, at 2 cun for severe ones, taking the point on both arms at once.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Renzong: soreness and distension. Dizong: soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation; on turning the needle, soreness and numbness spread through the chest and back and up to the vertex.
acupoints.application: Dizong is a key emergency point, no less effective than Renzhong, Baihui and Zusanli of the traditional twelve regular channels.
acupoints.notes: Renzong: among Tung's extraordinary points there is none identical with a point of the fourteen channels. Master Tung's book locates Renzong 3 cun above the crease, but 3 cun above would be Shouwuli of the fourteen channels, and the indications of Renzong and Shouwuli differ greatly; Master Tung evidently published in haste without revising. Following Master Hu, the location is corrected to 3.5 cun, which accords with Master Tung's intent. For many of Tung's extraordinary points the depth of insertion changes both the channel entered and the indications — this deserves particular attention, as the needling method for Renzong shows. Dizong: Master Tung's book gives 6 cun above the crease; for the same reason as with Renzong this is corrected here to 6.5 cun. Dizong is a key point among Tung's extraordinary points and belongs to both the 72 principal needlings and the 32 resolving needlings. Needling the three Zong points in a straight-line dao ma treats pain on the inner thigh and distending pain in the calf.
configNotes: In emergencies Shoujie may be added; Shoujie is easier to locate and is used more often in practice. For the emergency needling of cardiac paralysis and angina, add Dizong and Shou Xinling.

acupoints.code: IV.A.3. Upper arm, anterior – Zong zone
acupoints.name: Tianzong
acupoints.anatomy: Behind the cephalic vein; the circumflex humeral artery, the axillary nerve, the nerve of the six bowels and the nerve of the lower leg.
acupoints.location: In the depression between the lateral aspect of the humerus and the back of the biceps, 3 cun above Dizong.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver channel.
acupoints.properties: Clears heat and disinhibits damp, disinhibits and frees the lower burner.
acupoints.indications: Vaginal itching and vaginal pain, red and white vaginal discharge (remarkably effective), lower leg pain, sprained foot, poliomyelitis, body odour, diabetes.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: Tianzong lies near Jianzhong, and so is also effective for lower leg pain, sprained foot and poliomyelitis.

acupoints.code: IV.E.1. Shoulder – Shoulder zone 1
acupoints.name: Jianfeng
acupoints.anatomy: The deltoid, the brachial artery, branches of the cephalic vein, branches of the clavicular nerve, the branch nerve of the lung and the accessory cardiac nerve.
acupoints.location: With the arm raised, 0.5 cun below the centre of the hollow at the seam where the shoulder bone meets the arm bone.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Lung channels.
acupoints.properties: Quickens the blood and dispels stasis, frees the channels and quickens the connecting vessels.
acupoints.indications: High blood pressure, excessive sweating, breast cancer, breast lump, mastitis, inflammation of the nipple, paralysis of the upper limb, hemiparesis, hemiplegia, cerebral thrombosis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–0.8 cun; or oblique insertion from above downward, 0.8 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension and an electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: This point is specifically effective for breast cancer, mastitis and breast abscess; adding Shuanglong on the foot works remarkably well.

acupoints.code: IV.S.2. Shoulder – Jianbai zone
acupoints.name: Yunbai
acupoints.anatomy: Yunbai: the deltoid, the circumflex humeral artery, branches of the cephalic vein, branches of the clavicular nerve, the nerve of the six bowels and the accessory nerve of the lung. Libai: the accessory nerve of the kidney and the branch nerve of the lung.
acupoints.location: Yunbai: locate with the arm hanging down or the hand resting on the chest, in front of the shoulder joint about 2 cun from the tip of the shoulder — that is, 2 cun in front of Jianzhong. Libai: locate with the hand resting on the chest, 2 cun anterior to Jianzhong (the second point).
acupoints.meridian: Yunbai: enters the Liver and Kidney channels. Libai: enters the Liver channel.
acupoints.properties: Yunbai: regulates menstruation and the belt vessel, diffuses and frees the lower burner. Libai: soothes the sinews and quickens the connecting vessels.
acupoints.indications: Yunbai: vaginitis, metritis, ovaritis, vaginal itching, vaginal pain, red and white vaginal discharge, poliomyelitis, sprained foot (specifically effective). Libai: body odour, excessive sweating, sprained foot, foot pain, lower leg pain, poliomyelitis.
acupoints.technique: Yunbai: perpendicular insertion, 1–2 cun. Libai: perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: Yunbai, Libai, Jianzhong and Jianzhong (the second point) used together treat the lateral malleolus and arthritis of the ankle. Jianzhong paired with Yunbai treats calf pain, working in the same way as the three Zong points. For coma and loss of consciousness in stroke: Yunbai, Libai and Dizong. For vaginitis: Libai with Yunbai and Haibao. For difficult urination: Libai with Yunbai and the Lower Three Huang points (Tianhuang, Dihuang, Renhuang).

acupoints.code: IV.S.4. Shoulder – Shoulder zone 2
acupoints.name: Shenjian
acupoints.anatomy: The supraclavicular nerve, the axillary nerve, the branch nerve of the lung and the branch nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: At the midpoint of the line joining Jianfeng and Yunbai.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Liver channels.
acupoints.properties: Soothes the sinews and quickens the connecting vessels, frees the gates and disinhibits the orifices.
acupoints.indications: Poliomyelitis, cerebral haemorrhage, sequelae of cerebral thrombosis (hemiplegia), numbness of the arm, pain and numbness on the inner thigh.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.3–0.5 cun; or oblique insertion from above downward, 0.5–1 cun.
acupoints.notes: Shenjian is a key point among Tung's 72 principal needlings. Master Tung did not make it public in his book; Master Hu set it out on the basis of Master Tung's regular teaching. Any three of the points below the shoulder joint may be taken — as a vertical, horizontal or diagonal dao ma of three needles — to treat poliomyelitis and weakness of the legs.

acupoints.code: IV.L.1. Upper arm, lateral – Zhengji zone
acupoints.name: Zhengji yi, Zhengji er and Zhengji san
acupoints.anatomy: Accessory nerve of the liver, accessory nerve of the heart, spinal nerves.
acupoints.location: Locate with the arm hanging naturally. Zhengji yi lies on the midline of the lateral aspect of the humerus, 2 cun above the transverse elbow crease. Zhengji er is 2 cun above yi, and Zhengji san 2 cun above er.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Frees the channels and quickens the connecting vessels, soothes the sinews and disinhibits the bones.
acupoints.indications: Spinal periostitis (bone spurs), degenerative vertebral overgrowth, ankylosing spondylitis, sciatica, cervical bone spurs, hunchback, chronic pyelitis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun; or oblique insertion from below upward, 1–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness and distension with a marked numb, electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: The name Zhengji means to guide the spine (ji) back to true (zheng), because the point can realign the spine. Among Tung's points, those with a direct effect on the spine include Feixin, Erjiaoming, Wanshun, Zhengjin and Zhengzong. Combined with Guguan and Muguan this point treats conditions of the lumbar vertebrae.

acupoints.code: IV.P.1. Upper arm, posterior – Sanshen zone
acupoints.name: The Sanshen points
acupoints.anatomy: Accessory nerve of the kidney, accessory nerve of the liver, branch nerve of the lung.
acupoints.location: Locate with the hand resting on the chest. As described above for Sanshen yi, er and san.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Kidney and Lung channels.
acupoints.properties: Clears the lower burner, enriches the kidney and banks up the origin.
acupoints.indications: Proteinuria, pyelitis, impotence, premature ejaculation, lower back ache, lower back pain, pain from kidney stones, dry mouth, laryngitis, bronchitis, cough in the elderly, throat cancer, lung cancer.
acupoints.technique: Oblique insertion to 0.5 cun for dry mouth, which resolves at once. Oblique insertion to 1 cun for laryngitis, bronchitis, kidney depletion and similar conditions.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.application: Cough in the elderly is mostly a vacuity pattern, and as Sanshen enters the Kidney channel it has a regulating and supplementing action; in practice related supplementing points among Tung's extraordinary points may be added.
acupoints.notes: Shallow insertion enters the Lung channel, deep insertion the Kidney channel. This point resembles Houzhui, Shouying and Yuying in nature and indications, and they may substitute for one another. Sanshen is among Tung's 72 principal needlings and is also a supplementing point for the kidney. A straight-line dao ma needling works better still.

acupoints.code: IV.S.3. Shoulder – Qu zone
acupoints.name: Shangqu
acupoints.anatomy: Shangqu: the renal nerve and the accessory nerve of the liver. Xiaqu: the branch nerve of the lung and the branch nerve of the liver.
acupoints.location: Shangqu: on the back of the upper arm, 2 cun posterior to Jianzhong. Xiaqu: on the back of the arm, 2 cun below Shangqu — that is, 2 cun posterior to Jianzhong (the second point).
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver channel.
acupoints.properties: Soothes the sinews and quickens the connecting vessels.
acupoints.indications: Shangqu: poliomyelitis, sciatica, long-standing lower leg pain, strain of the groin and thigh, arm pain, high blood pressure. Xiaqu: sciatica (arising from impaired function of both lung and liver), hemiplegia, poliomyelitis, dislocation of a joint (from failure of the nerves), high blood pressure.
acupoints.technique: Shangqu: perpendicular insertion, 1–1.5 cun; or oblique insertion from above downward, 1.5–2 cun. Xiaqu: perpendicular insertion, 1–2 cun; or oblique insertion from below upward, 1.5–2 cun.

acupoints.code: XI.1. Back – Fenzhi zone
acupoints.name: Fenzhi shang
acupoints.anatomy: Secretory nerve; hepatic nerve.
acupoints.location: On the shoulder and back, 1 cun directly below the fork between the scapula and the humerus.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver, Lung and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Clears the liver and resolves toxin.
acupoints.indications: Drug poisoning; venom from snakes, scorpions, centipedes and other creatures; body odour, bad breath, diabetes, rabid dog bite, painful urination, blood strangury, gonorrhoea, syphilis, food poisoning, attempted suicide by poison (mild cases are treatable, severe ones hard to treat), generalised itching, chest pain.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–1.5 cun.
acupoints.notes: Fenzhi shang, Fenzhi zhong and Fenzhi xia are among Tung's 32 resolving points and are key detoxifying points. They properly belong with the points of the back among Tung's extraordinary points; since points on the back are mostly treated by bloodletting and this book does not include the chest, abdomen and back groups, they are placed in the 4-4 region because they lie close to the arm.

acupoints.code: XI.1. Back – Fenzhi zone
acupoints.name: Fenzhi xia
acupoints.anatomy: Secretory nerve; branch nerve of the lung; mammary nerve.
acupoints.location: 1.5 cun directly below Fenzhi shang.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver, Lung and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Clears the liver and resolves toxin.
acupoints.indications: As for Fenzhi shang; it also treats mastitis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–1.5 cun.
acupoints.application: Spot-pricking this group to bleed also works well.
acupoints.notes: Fenzhi xia properly belongs with the points of the back among Tung's extraordinary points. Master Tung needled the hands and feet, generally not the chest, abdomen or back, where he used a three-edged needle instead; but this point lies at the junction of the upper arm and the back and is an important one. Since this book deals only with the ten regional groups and leaves other points aside, it is included in the 4-4 region.

acupoints.code: XI.1. Back – Fenzhi zone
acupoints.name: Fenzhi zhong
acupoints.anatomy: Secretory nerve; branch nerve of the lung; mammary nerve.
acupoints.location: 0.6 cun medial to Fenzhi xia.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver, Lung and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Clears the liver and resolves toxin.
acupoints.indications: As for Fenzhi shang; it also treats mastitis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–1.5 cun.
acupoints.application: Taking Fenzhi shang, zhong and xia together, all three needles form the triangular needling characteristic of Tung's dao ma method, and their effects multiply.
acupoints.notes: Fenzhi zhong is not explicitly listed in Master Tung's book and was made public by Master Hu in his writings. Fenzhi shang, zhong and xia are all among Tung's 32 resolving needlings; their detoxifying power is considerable and they are also effective in treating venereal disease. The point properly belongs to the region of the back, where ninety per cent of Tung's points are treated primarily by bloodletting; only the Fenzhi points are treated primarily by needling, though bloodletting is also possible. As they lie at the junction of the arm and the back, and this book does not discuss bloodletting at points on the back, the Fenzhi points are covered here with the arm.

acupoints.code: Huobao: V.Pl.1. Toes, plantar – Huobao zone · Fuling: V.Pl.2. Toes, plantar – Fuling zone
acupoints.name: Huobao, Fuling yi and Fuling er
acupoints.location: Lying flat: Huobao is at the centre of the crease of the distal interphalangeal joint of the second toe on the sole. Below it, on either side of the crease of the metatarsophalangeal joint, are Fuling yi and er.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver channel.
acupoints.properties: Courses the liver and rectifies qi.
acupoints.indications: Heart pain, liver disease, difficult labour, retained placenta, terminating a pregnancy (specifically effective), red and white vaginal discharge. Fuling additionally treats tumours and inflammation of the uterus and ovaries, and gynaecological conditions such as irregular menstruation.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.3–0.5 cun. Pricking with a bloodletting needle to release dark blood brings an immediate effect.
acupoints.notes: Among Tung's extraordinary points, those given specifically to gynaecological conditions — the five Fuke points, Fengchao, Jiemei and other key gynaecological points — mostly belong to the Liver channel.

acupoints.code: V.Dl.1. Second toe, dorsal – Mufu zone
acupoints.name: Mufu
acupoints.anatomy: Accessory cardiac nerve; nerve of the six bowels.
acupoints.location: 0.3 cun lateral to the exact centre of the second segment of the second toe.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver channel.
acupoints.properties: Regulates menstruation and the belt vessel, harmonises the thoroughfare and conception vessels.
acupoints.indications: Red and white vaginal discharge, irregular menstruation, menstrual pain, metritis, blocked fallopian tubes.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.2–0.4 cun, close against the bone; a fine 0.5-cun filiform needle hurts less.
acupoints.notes: Needling points on the fingers and toes is painful, and most people find it hard to bear; but points on the hands and feet respond strongly and treat well, which is why some practitioners work with hand needling alone and get very good results. Needling the fingers and toes does hurt, but if the patient is asked to breathe in deeply and forcefully as the needle goes in — drawing a full breath and holding it — the insertion is less painful. This is offered for what it is worth.

acupoints.code: V.M.1. Big toe, medial – Haibao zone
acupoints.name: Haibao
acupoints.anatomy: Extensor hallucis longus, the superficial peroneal nerve and the branch nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: On the medial side of the big toe, at the midpoint of the interphalangeal joint, just behind the medial edge of the nail.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Liver channels.
acupoints.properties: Scatters stasis and frees the connecting vessels.
acupoints.indications: Keratitis, hernia, vaginitis, finger pain.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.1–0.3 cun.

acupoints.code: VI.Pl.6. Metatarsals, plantar – Shangliu zone
acupoints.name: Shangliu
acupoints.anatomy: General nerve of the hindbrain (cerebellum).
acupoints.location: Lying flat, at the centre of the front edge of the hard skin of the heel on the sole.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart channel.
acupoints.properties: Clears heat and opens the orifices, fortifies the brain and quiets the spirit.
acupoints.indications: Brain tumour, hydrocephalus, pain in the cerebellum, neuralgia of the cranial nerves, neurasthenia, brain cancer.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.3–0.5 cun.
acupoints.application: Master Hu combined this point with Waisanguan, Sanzhong and Zhengnao yi, er and san to cure an American patient with brain cancer who had been treated without success for more than three years at a hospital in Hawaii; after twenty-nine needlings by Master Hu the patient recovered. For concussion with loss of consciousness: this point combined with Zhengjin, Zhengzong, Zhenjing, Zhenghui and Sanzhong, needles retained for two hours, with bloodletting near the area below the medial malleolus — effective.

acupoints.code: VI.Pl.5. Metatarsals, plantar – Sansheng zone
acupoints.name: The Sansheng points
acupoints.anatomy: Branches of the plantar nerves, the nerve of the heart, the accessory nerve of the kidney, the cranial nerves.
acupoints.location: As described above for Sansheng yi, er and san.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Calms the liver and boosts the kidney.
acupoints.indications: High blood pressure (specifically effective), excessively high diastolic pressure (specifically effective), cerebral haemorrhage, cerebral thrombosis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun.
acupoints.notes: This is a key point among Tung's extraordinary points and one of Tung's 72 principal needlings, with a marked effect in regulating blood pressure. Master Tung did not make Sansheng public in his book; Master Hu supplied it on the basis of what Master Tung taught day to day. In treating blood pressure, combining it with bloodletting at the relevant areas works better still.

acupoints.code: VI.Dl.1. Metatarsals, dorsal – Foot Huo zone
acupoints.name: Huoying
acupoints.anatomy: Huoying: the cardiac nerve and the accessory nerve of the liver. Huozhu: the branch nerve of the heart, the cardiac artery, and branches of the sensory peroneal nerve.
acupoints.location: Huoying: at the front edge of the first and second metatarsals, 0.5 cun up in the seam between the bones at the middle of the metatarsophalangeal joint. Huozhu: at the lower border of the fork between the first and second metatarsals.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Liver channels.
acupoints.properties: Huoying: frees and disinhibits the waterways, strengthens the heart and settles palpitations. Huozhu: frees and disinhibits the lower burner, soothes the liver and rectifies qi.
acupoints.indications: Huoying: palpitations, dizziness, retained placenta, enlargement of the bones, pain in the lower jaw (difficulty opening the mouth), strengthening the heart (used in states of coma), metritis, uterine fibroid. It can terminate a pregnancy. Huozhu: enlargement of the bones, headache arising from heart disease, liver disease, neurasthenia, cardiac paralysis, pain in the hands and feet, metritis, uterine fibroid. It can terminate a pregnancy and may be used in difficult labour.
acupoints.technique: Huoying: perpendicular insertion, 0.3–0.5 cun, or oblique insertion, 0.3–0.5 cun. Huozhu: perpendicular insertion, 0.3–1 cun. For pain in the hands and feet, use the right point for the left side and the left point for the right.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Huoying: soreness, distension and pain. Huozhu: local soreness and distension.

acupoints.code: VI.Dl.2. Metatarsals, dorsal – Foot Jin zone
acupoints.name: Menjin
acupoints.anatomy: Extensor digitorum brevis, the dorsal venous network of the foot, the second dorsal metatarsal artery, the dorsal digital nerves, the duodenal nerve, the branch nerve of the stomach and the uterine nerve.
acupoints.location: At the front edge of the fork between the second and third metatarsals.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Stomach, Large Intestine and Small Intestine channels.
acupoints.properties: Regulates the spleen and stomach, transforms stasis and relieves pain.
acupoints.indications: Cramping and gripping pain before and after menstruation, enteritis, gastritis, abdominal distension, abdominal pain, appendicitis.
acupoints.technique: Use a fine filiform needle, perpendicular insertion to 0.5 cun.
acupoints.notes: Menjin with Menjin xia (0.5 cun above Neiting) as a dao ma, combined with Sima and Sanzhong, is effective for rhinitis, tinnitus and migraine. Menjin and Menjin xia as a dao ma with Sizhi treats aching numbness of the middle finger. Menjin with Shuiqu and Huozhu as a horizontal three-needle dao ma is effective for headache and uterine conditions.

acupoints.code: VI.Dl.3. Metatarsals, dorsal – Foot Mu zone
acupoints.name: Mudou
acupoints.anatomy: Splenic nerve, hepatic nerve.
acupoints.location: Mudou: at the upper border of the third and fourth metatarsals, in the seam between the bones at the upper border of the metatarsophalangeal joint. Muliu: in the depression at the front edge of the junction of the third and fourth metatarsals.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver and Spleen channels.
acupoints.properties: Mudou: fortifies the spleen and transforms damp, courses the liver and harmonises the stomach. Muliu: harmonises the spleen and stomach, courses the liver and disinhibits the gallbladder.
acupoints.indications: Mudou: splenomegaly (glomus lump), indigestion, liver disease, fatigue, gallbladder conditions, poliomyelitis. Muliu: leukocyte disorders, splenomegaly, indigestion, liver disease, fatigue, gallbladder conditions, poliomyelitis, hemiparesis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.3–0.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Mudou: soreness, distension and pain. Muliu: soreness and distension.
acupoints.notes: Mudou is seldom used alone and is mostly paired with Muliu. Both enter the Liver and Spleen channels and so act on both organs. In practice the Upper Three Huang points (Tianhuang, Minghuang, Qihuang) and Ganmen are used more often for liver conditions, while these points are taken for the spleen.

acupoints.code: VI.Dl.4. Metatarsals, dorsal – Foot Shui zone
acupoints.name: Liuwan
acupoints.anatomy: Branch nerve of the lung; branch nerve of the kidney.
acupoints.location: Liuwan: in the seam between the bones at the upper border of the fourth and fifth metatarsophalangeal joints. Shuiqu: at the front edge of the junction of the fourth and fifth metatarsals; 0.3 cun below it is Diwuhui of the Foot Shaoyang Gallbladder channel.
acupoints.meridian: Liuwan: enters the Liver and Gallbladder channels. Shuiqu: enters the Liver and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Liuwan: courses the liver and rectifies qi, soothes the sinews and quickens the connecting vessels. Shuiqu: frees the channels and quickens the connecting vessels, moves qi and relieves pain.
acupoints.indications: Liuwan: stopping bleeding (including bleeding from a fall or a knife wound, or bleeding that will not stop after an injection), migraine. Shuiqu: lower back pain, oedema of the four limbs, abdominal distension, neuralgia of the neck, sciatica.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.3–0.5 cun.

acupoints.code: VI.M.1. Foot, medial – Foot medial Huo zone
acupoints.name: Hualian
acupoints.anatomy: Hualian: the proper plantar digital nerve, the dorsal digital artery, the branch nerve of the heart and the accessory branch nerve of the kidney. Huoju: the proper plantar digital nerve, the dorsal digital artery, the branch nerve of the heart and the accessory nerve of the kidney. Huosan: the branch nerve of the heart, the accessory nerve of the kidney and the accessory nerve of the six bowels.
acupoints.location: Hualian: on the medial border of the foot, 2 cun behind the first metatarsophalangeal joint; locate lying flat. Huoju: on the medial side of the first metatarsal, 1 cun behind Hualian — 3 cun above the metatarsophalangeal joint. Huosan: on the medial side of the first metatarsal, 1 cun behind Huoju — 4 cun above the metatarsophalangeal joint.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Clears and drains heart fire, opens the orifices and rouses the brain.
acupoints.indications: Hualian: dizziness, blurred vision and palpitations from high blood pressure, cardiac weakness, brain tumour, meningitis. Huoju: numbness of the hand, palpitations, dizziness, foot pain, high blood pressure, a heavy distended feeling in the head, blurred vision, aching eyelids from raised intraocular pressure, inability to turn the neck freely, brain tumour, meningitis. Huosan: headache, distension in the head, keratitis, lower back ache from kidney depletion, dizziness, blurred vision, back pain, brain tumour, meningitis.
acupoints.technique: Transverse insertion, 0.5–1 cun. Insert the needle at right angles to the metatarsal, running along the lower border of the bone.
acupoints.application: Hualian, Huoju and Huosan together are specifically effective for brain tumour and meningitis, and also treat neurasthenia. For brain tumour and meningitis: Zhengjin, Zhengzong, Sanzhong, Linggu, Dabai, Zhenghui, Qianhui.
acupoints.notes: Master Tung's book places Hualian 1.5 cun behind the metatarsophalangeal joint, which led some to take it for Taibai; but the two belong to different channels and differ in nature and indications, so the point is given here as 2 cun behind the joint, in keeping with what Master Tung taught day to day. Hualian, Huoju and Huosan form a straight-line dao ma and in practice all three may be needled together. In the five phases the heart governs fire, and the heart also connects with the brain, so these three needles act strongly on the brain; taking the points on one foot is enough. If a purplish-blue vessel shows over a point, a bloodletting needle may be used there to break up blood and move qi, which opens the orifices and rouses the brain. Taibai and Gongsun belong to the Foot Taiyin Spleen channel of the fourteen channels and their nature is to regulate the spleen and stomach, whereas Tung's Hualian, Huoju and Huosan belong to the Heart and Kidney channels, treat chiefly conditions of the brain, and are opening-the-orifices, rousing-the-brain points. The two sets differ in channel, nature and indications, each with its own field; the reason they are distinct points is plain, and confusing Tung's extraordinary points with points of the fourteen channels is a serious misunderstanding. The three points may be taken together as a vertical three-needle dao ma for a stronger effect. All three are needled close against the bone; because their action is strong they must not be taken on both feet at once, and they are contraindicated in pregnancy for fear of miscarriage.

acupoints.code: VI.M.2. Foot, medial – Foot medial Shui zone 1
acupoints.name: Shuixiang and Shuixian
acupoints.anatomy: Branch nerve of the kidney; cranial nerves.
acupoints.location: Directly behind the medial malleolus, 0.5 cun below the depression close against the bone at the front border of the Achilles tendon. Shuixian is 2 cun directly below Shuixiang.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Kidney channel.
acupoints.properties: Disinhibits water and disperses swelling, frees and regulates the thoroughfare and conception vessels.
acupoints.indications: Nephritis, oedema of the four limbs, lower back pain from kidney depletion, pain in the vertebrae, postpartum wind conditions, cataract.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.3–0.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: If a dark discolouration appears over the area of Shuixiang, Shuixian and Shuijing, a bloodletting needle may first be used at that point, which helps to free the channels and quicken the connecting vessels.

acupoints.code: VI.Pl.1. Metatarsals, plantar – Huagu 1 zone
acupoints.name: The Huagu yi points
acupoints.anatomy: Medial plantar nerve; nerves of the spleen, lung and kidney; hepatic nerve.
acupoints.location: On the sole between the first and second metatarsals: one point 0.5 cun from the web between the toes, one 0.5 cun behind it, one 0.5 cun behind that, and one 0.5 cun behind that again — four points in all.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver channel.
acupoints.properties: Soothes the liver and resolves constraint, clears the liver and brightens the eyes.
acupoints.indications: Trachoma, keratitis, blepharitis, tearing in the wind, photophobia, aching distending pain in the brow ridge, pain in the nasal bone, headache, toothache, tinnitus, deafness.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun.
acupoints.application: Huagu yi is made up of four separate points; in practice taking any two of them gives a good result.
acupoints.notes: As the point lies on the sole, insert quickly, and have the patient draw a deep breath while using a No. 36 needle to lessen the pain. Keratitis: this point may be needled alone without other points, retaining the needle for an hour; the redness and swelling will subside. Tearing in the wind: combine this point with Zhuyuan on the hand, adding the Upper Three Huang points and the Lower Three Huang points. Tinnitus: this point with Wanshun yi and er, Sima, Sanzhong and the Lower Three Huang points. Eye conditions: thread from Huoying through to Huagu.

acupoints.code: VI.Pl.3. Metatarsals, plantar – Huagu 3 zone
acupoints.name: Huagu san
acupoints.anatomy: Splenic nerve.
acupoints.location: On the sole between the third and fourth metatarsals, 2 cun from the web between the toes.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Frees the channels and quickens the connecting vessels, moves qi and relieves pain.
acupoints.indications: Lower back pain, sciatica, pain in the vertebrae.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun.
acupoints.application: Huagu san with Huagu yi, Shuijin and Shuitong treats lower back pain. Zhongbai, Shangbai, Jianzhong and Huagu san treat sciatica. Zhengji, Huagu san and Shuixiang treat pain in the vertebrae. For a herniated intervertebral disc, bleed at the site of the problem, then needle Huagu san combined with the Upper Three Huang points and the Lower Three Huang points, or with Zhengji yi, er and san, adding or subtracting points according to the presentation. Combining this with spinal manipulation is best.
acupoints.notes: Huagu san connects with Mudou and Muliu and is effective for weakness of the middle and ring fingers with inability to bend or extend them. Huagu san corresponds to the area of the three Huo points and the three Xing points on the opposite hand.

acupoints.code: VI.Pl.4. Metatarsals, plantar – Huagu 4 zone
acupoints.name: Huagu si
acupoints.anatomy: Nerve of the lung; nerve of the kidney.
acupoints.location: On the sole between the fourth and fifth metatarsals, 1.5 cun from the web between the toes; it connects with Liuwan.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Lung and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Frees the channels and quickens the connecting vessels, frees and disinhibits the lower burner.
acupoints.indications: Pain in the vertebrae, sciatica, lower abdominal pain, stomach pain, stopping bleeding, constipation, irregular menstruation, swelling of the dorsum of the foot, red eyes, bedwetting, frequent urination.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun.

acupoints.code: VII.P.1. Lower leg, posterior – Zheng zone
acupoints.name: Zhengjin and Zhengzong
acupoints.anatomy: General nerve of the vertebrae, general nerve of the brain; tibial nerve.
acupoints.location: Zhengjin lies at the exact centre of the Achilles tendon, 3.5 cun from the sole. Zhengzong is 2 cun above Zhengjin.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Kidney and Bladder channels.
acupoints.properties: Clears heat and rouses the brain, frees qi and relieves pain.
acupoints.indications: Lumbar spine pain, acute lumbar sprain, sharp pain in the vertebrae, bone spurs of the neck with inability to turn the head and pain in the neck sinews, enlargement of the cranial bones, hydrocephalus, wrenched qi, occipital headache.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun (the effect is better still if the needle passes through the Achilles tendon). Robust patients may be needled seated; frail patients should lie on their side before insertion.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.

acupoints.code: VII.P.1. Lower leg, posterior – Zheng zone
acupoints.name: Zhengshi
acupoints.anatomy: Branch nerve of the lung, general nerve of the vertebrae, tibial nerve.
acupoints.location: At the exact centre of the Achilles tendon, 2 cun above Zhengzong.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Kidney and Bladder channels.
acupoints.properties: Courses and guides the channels and connecting vessels, moves qi and quickens the blood.
acupoints.indications: Shoulder and back pain, lower back pain, sciatica, acute lumbar sprain and wrenched qi, headache.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun.
acupoints.notes: Zhengjin, Zhengzong and Zhengshi may be needled together as a vertical three-needle dao ma for a stronger effect; both the vertebrae and the head (with Sanzhong added) benefit from this treatment.

acupoints.code: VII.L.4. Lower leg, lateral – Sanzhong zone
acupoints.name: The Sanzhong points
acupoints.anatomy: Lateral sural cutaneous nerve, branch nerve of the heart, branch nerve of the lung, splenic nerve.
acupoints.location: Sanzhong yi: 3 cun directly above the tip of the lateral malleolus, then 1 cun forward. Sanzhong er: 2 cun directly above Sanzhong yi. Sanzhong san: 2 cun directly above Sanzhong er.
acupoints.meridian: Sanzhong yi: enters the Heart, Lung and Spleen channels. Sanzhong er: enters the Heart, Lung and Spleen channels. Sanzhong san: enters the Heart, Liver, Spleen and Lung channels.
acupoints.properties: Breaks qi and moves the blood, eliminates accumulation and disperses stasis.
acupoints.indications: Goitre (arising from heart disease), protruding eyeballs, tonsillitis, deviation of the mouth and eye (facial nerve paralysis), migraine, glomus lumps, liver disease, brain tumour, brain cancer, meningitis, laryngitis, splenomegaly, inflammation of the spleen.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–2 cun; or spot-pricked to bleed with a bloodletting needle.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: Needling Sanzhong yi, er and san at the same time forms a vertical dao ma with the power to move qi and break blood, free the orifices and quiet the spirit; the right needling combination speeds the effect considerably. Sanzhong and Waisanguan are both key points for tumours, and in practice either group may be chosen and combined with related points. Main points for treating cancer: the Upper Three Huang points, the Lower Three Huang points, Linggu, Dabai, and responsive points wherever they appear, combined with other relevant points. In holographic terms the responsive area of the Sanzhong group falls exactly at the head and the front of the shoulder. Master Lai records in his book that Master Tung used Sanzhong effectively for breast lumps and for the early stages of oesophageal cancer and cancer of the sublingual gland. As Sanzhong breaks qi and moves the blood, it can be included in the point combination for any tumour.

acupoints.code: VII.A.4. Lower leg, anterior – Sihua zone
acupoints.name: Sihua shang
acupoints.anatomy: Sihua shang: nerve of the six bowels, branch nerve of the lung, branch nerve of the heart. Sihua zhong: nerve of the six bowels, branch nerve of the heart, branch nerve of the lung, accessory nerve of the six bowels. Sihua xia: nerve of the six bowels, accessory nerve of the six bowels, accessory nerve of the lung, accessory nerve of the kidney.
acupoints.location: Sihua shang: 3 cun below the lateral eye of the knee, in the depression close against the bone at the lateral border of the tibia. Sihua zhong: 4.5 cun directly below Sihua shang, 1.2 cun lateral to Sihua li — that is, 0.5 cun above Tiaokou of the fourteen channels (8 cun below the eye of the knee). Sihua xia: 2.5 cun directly below Sihua fu.
acupoints.meridian: Sihua shang: enters the Heart, Lung and Stomach channels. Sihua zhong: enters the Heart, Lung and Stomach channels. Sihua xia: enters the Lung, Kidney and Stomach channels.
acupoints.properties: Sihua shang: courses the heart and clears the lung, regulates the spleen and stomach. Sihua zhong: courses the heart and clears the lung, regulates the spleen and stomach. Sihua xia: rectifies the spleen and harmonises the stomach.
acupoints.indications: Sihua shang: asthma, toothache, palpitations, growths in the mouth, dizziness, heart disease, cholera with cramping, duodenal ulcer. Sihua zhong: asthma, eye conditions (aching pain, keratitis, conjunctivitis, cataract), endocarditis, angina, myocardial infarction, hardening of the cardiac vessels, pain on both sides of the heart, cardiac paralysis, chest oppression, acute gastroenteritis, dispersing swelling of the bones; lung cancer, emphysema, pneumonia. Sihua xia: enteritis, abdominal distension, stomach pain, oedema of the lower limbs, teeth-grinding in sleep.
acupoints.technique: Sihua shang: perpendicular insertion, 2–3 cun. At 2 cun it treats asthma; at 3 cun, heart disease. Sihua zhong: perpendicular insertion, 2–3 cun, for asthma and eye conditions. Spot-pricking to bleed with a bloodletting needle works remarkably for hardening of the cardiac vessels, acute gastroenteritis, chest oppression and pleurisy. Sihua xia: perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun; or spot-pricked to bleed with a bloodletting needle.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Sihua shang: soreness and distension. Sihua zhong: local soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation. Sihua xia: local soreness and distension.
acupoints.application: Needling is not always required in the area of Sihua shang, Sihua zhong, Sihua li and Sihua xia; if a dark bluish vessel shows there, bloodletting with a bloodletting needle works remarkably for heart conditions, acute gastrointestinal conditions and chest oppression.
acupoints.notes: The Sihua points regulate and supplement qi — specifically the qi of the spleen and stomach. Sima is the key point group for qi disorders, and what it regulates is the qi of the heart and lung. Linggu and Dabai move qi, quicken the blood and transform stasis, and what they regulate is likewise the qi of the heart and lung, promoting the flow of construction and defence. Sihua shang, zhong and xia, arranged from above downward, form a holographic projection of the organs, with the knee as the head: shang governs the upper burner, the heart and lung; zhong governs the middle burner, the spleen and stomach; xia governs the lower burner, the intestines and lower abdomen. Needling all three as a Tung dao ma frees the triple burner and the five viscera and regulates the functioning of the whole body — a hallmark of Tung's needling.

acupoints.code: VII.A.4. Lower leg, anterior – Sihua zone
acupoints.name: Sihua fu
acupoints.anatomy: As for Sihua zhong: nerve of the six bowels, branch nerve of the heart, branch nerve of the lung, accessory nerve of the six bowels.
acupoints.location: 2.5 cun directly below Sihua zhong; 1 cun below Xiajuxu of the fourteen channels.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart, Lung and Stomach channels.
acupoints.properties: Courses the heart and rectifies the lung, regulates the spleen and stomach.
acupoints.indications: As for Sihua zhong.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–2 cun.
acupoints.application: At Sihua shang, Sihua zhong and Sihua fu, if a bluish vessel is visible it may be pricked to bleed — dark blood is the sign to look for — which treats heart disease and gastrointestinal conditions.
acupoints.notes: Rheumatic pain in the legs: spot-prick to bleed at Sihua shang, Sihua zhong and Sihua fu, combined with bloodletting at the site of the problem, then needle the Upper Three Huang points, Zhongjiuli, Tongxin, Tongguan and Linggu. Bleeding the Sihua points with a three-edged needle and then taking Linggu, Dabai and Sima treats emphysema. Lung cancer: first bleed the heart and lung region of the back with a bloodletting needle, take responsive points on the palm and the inner forearm, then take Linggu and Dabai — effective, and dietary therapy must be combined with it. Pain in the upper teeth: Sihua, Shousanchi and Linggu may be taken. Sihua fu, Sihua xia and Fuchang may be needled together as a dao ma, effective for lower abdominal pain and enteritis.

acupoints.code: VII.A.4. Lower leg, anterior – Sihua zone
acupoints.name: Sihua wai
acupoints.anatomy: Lateral sural cutaneous nerve, branch nerve of the lung, nerve of the six bowels.
acupoints.location: 1.5 cun lateral to Sihua zhong.
acupoints.meridian: The Lung and Stomach channels.
acupoints.properties: Quickens the blood and dispels wind, disperses inflammation and settles pain.
acupoints.indications: Acute enteritis, toothache, migraine, facial nerve paralysis (deviation of the mouth and eye), pleurisy.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–1.5 cun.
acupoints.application: Spot-pricking with a bloodletting needle to release dark blood treats acute gastroenteritis, pleurisy, distension in the chest, asthma, sciatica, shoulder and arm pain, earache, chronic rhinitis, headache and high blood pressure (see Master Tung Ching-chang's Orthodox Extraordinary Points of Tung's Acupuncture).
acupoints.notes: Sihua zhong, Sihua wai and Zuqianjin needled together form a horizontal three-needle group given to conditions of the middle burner, effective for appendicular pain and acute gastroenteritis.

acupoints.code: VII.A.4. Lower leg, anterior – Sihua zone
acupoints.name: Fuchang
acupoints.anatomy: Lateral sural cutaneous nerve, nerve of the six bowels, accessory nerve of the lung, renal nerve, accessory nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: 1.5 cun directly below Sihua xia.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Stomach and Large Intestine channels.
acupoints.properties: Regulates the intestines and stomach, clears heat and disinhibits damp.
acupoints.indications: As for Sihua xia.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun (with a fine filiform needle); or spot-pricked to bleed with a bloodletting needle.
acupoints.notes: This point usually accompanies Sihua xia and acts quickly, but it is not used on its own (see Master Tung's book). For cardiac enlargement, medication alone gives little result; bleeding first around the Sihua points and the heart and lung region of the back, then needling, works well.

acupoints.code: VII.M.1. Lower leg, medial – Lower Three Huang zone
acupoints.name: Tianhuang
acupoints.anatomy: Saphenous nerve, renal nerve, nerve of the six bowels, branch nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: 1 cun directly below the lower border of the medial tibial condyle of the knee — that is, 1 cun directly below Yinlingquan of the fourteen channels.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Clears heat and transforms damp, courses and guides the lower burner.
acupoints.indications: Excess stomach acid, nausea and regurgitation, nephritis, diabetes, proteinuria, cystitis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.application: Combined with Tianhuang fu it treats nausea and regurgitation and excess stomach acid.

acupoints.code: VII.M.1. Lower leg, medial – Lower Three Huang zone
acupoints.name: Tianhuang fu
acupoints.anatomy: Saphenous nerve, nerve of the six bowels.
acupoints.location: 1.5 cun directly below Tianhuang, on the medial side of the tibia.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Spleen and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Regulates qi and frees the channels, boosts the kidney and fortifies the spleen.
acupoints.indications: Excess stomach acid, nausea and regurgitation, deviation of the eyeball, astigmatism, anaemia, epilepsy, mental illness, aching pain in the brow ridge, pain in the nasal bone, dizziness, kidney depletion, sciatica, lower back pain. (Effective for all conditions arising from kidney depletion.)
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun. When used to supplement the kidney, needle to 2 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: Tianhuang fu is also called Shenguan. It treats all conditions arising from kidney depletion and is a supplementing point for kidney qi — one of the few key kidney-supplementing points among Tung's extraordinary points. Needled perpendicularly Shenguan connects with the heart; needled obliquely outward it connects with the kidney. Its depth may likewise be divided into three layers: the shallow layer treats sciatica, the middle layer the lower back and kidney, and the deep layer the head — the region treated changing with the depth. Master Tung had a well-known case in which he used Shenguan on the opposite side to treat deviation of the eyeball caused by a mistaken acupuncture insertion.

acupoints.code: VII.M.1. Lower leg, medial – Lower Three Huang zone
acupoints.name: Dihuang
acupoints.anatomy: Saphenous nerve, medial sural cutaneous nerve, renal nerve.
acupoints.location: 7.5 cun directly above the upper border of the medial malleolus — that is, 4 cun directly above Renhuang, and 0.5 cun above Lougu of the fourteen channels.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Courses the liver and resolves constraint, supplements the kidney and boosts qi.
acupoints.indications: Nephritis, oedema of the four limbs, diabetes, gonorrhoea, impotence, premature ejaculation, seminal emission, nocturnal emission, proteinuria, blood in the urine, uterine fibroid, irregular menstruation, lower back pain from kidney depletion.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–2 cun.
acupoints.application: Tianhuang, Dihuang and Renhuang together are called the Lower Three Huang points. Sometimes Tianhuang fu, Dihuang and Renhuang are also called the Lower Three Huang; combined with Tongshen and Tongbei they are specifically effective for kidney depletion, nephritis and diabetes.
acupoints.notes: Take one dao ma group — either the Lower Three Huang, or Tongshen, Tongbei and Tongwei — then add the Upper Three Huang points, Shuijin and Shuitong, with moxa at the Weimao qi points, the Fuchao twenty-three points, the kidney-water region of the lower back, and Sihua shang; sustained over a long course this treats diabetes with good results. The Lower Three Huang points are the well-known strengthening, kidney-supplementing points of Tung's acupuncture; needled together with the Upper Three Huang points over a long period they regulate and supplement original qi and build up the constitution. Taking the Lower Three Huang with the Upper Three Huang, Sanzhong, and Tongguan, Tongshan and Tongtian, occasionally needling Tung's responsive points on the back, sometimes bleeding at Zhenghui, and needling Zhengjin, Zhengzong and Zhengshi — this combination has cured several cases of epilepsy in the author's own practice, with considerable success over a three-month course.

acupoints.code: VII.M.1. Lower leg, medial – Lower Three Huang zone
acupoints.name: Renhuang
acupoints.anatomy: Saphenous nerve, branch nerve of the kidney, branch nerve of the lung.
acupoints.location: 3.5 cun directly above the upper border of the medial malleolus — that is, 0.5 cun directly above Sanyinjiao of the fourteen channels, on the medial side of the tibia.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Lung and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Harmonises the blood and soothes the sinews, supplements the kidney and boosts the essence.
acupoints.indications: Gonorrhoea, impotence, premature ejaculation, seminal emission, seminal efflux, pain in the lumbar vertebrae, neck pain, dizziness, numbness of the hand, diabetes, blood in the urine, pyelitis, cystitis, lower back pain and back pain from kidney depletion.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.6–1.5 cun. Oblique insertion upward is specifically effective for back pain, arm pain and neck pain (use a 2-cun needle inserted close against the bone).
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.application: This point strengthens the essence and the constitution. It may serve as an anaesthetic point in surgery of the gallbladder and spleen (noted for reference only).

acupoints.code: VII.L.1. Lower leg, lateral – Sanli zone
acupoints.name: Cesanli and Cexiasanli
acupoints.anatomy: Lateral sural cutaneous nerve, dental nerve, branch nerve of the lung.
acupoints.location: Cesanli lies at the front border of the fibula — 2.5 cun lateral to Sihua shang. Cexiasanli is 2 cun below Cesanli.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Lung channels.
acupoints.properties: Quickens the blood and dispels stasis, disperses inflammation and relieves pain.
acupoints.indications: Toothache, facial neuralgia, trigeminal neuralgia, migraine, intercostal neuralgia, pain of appendicitis.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.notes: For migraine, goitre, swelling under the tongue and similar conditions this point works as Sanzhong does; the two may be used in alternation with Sima, with good results.

acupoints.code: VII.L.2. Lower leg, lateral – Zuwujin – Zuqianjin zone
acupoints.name: Zuqianjin and Zuwujin
acupoints.anatomy: Lateral sural cutaneous nerve, branch nerve of the lung, branch nerve of the kidney, nerve of the side of the throat.
acupoints.location: Zuqianjin lies at the front border of the fibula — 0.5 cun lateral to Cexiasanli and then 2 cun directly below it. Zuwujin is 2 cun below Zuqianjin.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Lung and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Drains lung heat, disinhibits the throat.
acupoints.indications: A fish bone stuck in the throat, laryngitis, sores in the throat, tonsillitis, goitre, appendicular pain, acute enteritis, shoulder and back pain.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1 cun; or spot-pricked to bleed with a bloodletting needle.
acupoints.notes: In terms of the channels, Zuqianjin and Zuwujin connect with the Yang Linking vessel, which arises on the lateral side of the heel, passes upward over the lateral malleolus, and runs from behind the axilla over the shoulder to the forehead. Besides treating disorders of the Yang Linking vessel, these points also treat conditions of the neck, particularly those of the respiratory tract.

acupoints.code: VII.L.3. Lower leg, lateral – Waisanguan zone
acupoints.name: The Waisanguan points
acupoints.anatomy: Lateral sural cutaneous nerve, nerve of the lung, branch nerve of the liver.
acupoints.location: Waisanguan er is at the midpoint of the line joining the tip of the lateral malleolus and the high bone on the lateral side of the knee. Waisanguan yi is at the midpoint between Waisanguan er and the tip of the lateral malleolus. Waisanguan san is at the midpoint between Waisanguan er and the lateral side of the knee.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Lung and Liver channels.
acupoints.properties: Disperses stasis and dissipates binds, diffuses and frees qi and blood.
acupoints.indications: Laryngitis, throat cancer, lung cancer, tonsillitis, mumps, rosacea, acne, comedones, scrofula, shoulder and arm pain, tumours and cancers, abdominal tumours, breast cancer.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 1–1.5 cun; or spot-pricking with a bloodletting needle to release dark blood, which works well.
acupoints.notes: Waisanguan functions as Sanzhong does and is an essential point for any benign or malignant tumour and for red inflamed acne; the two groups may also be used in alternation. Lying on the lateral aspect of the lower leg, the point corresponds to the arm, and so is effective for numbness and pain in the arm, shoulder and back pain, and weakness of the arm.

acupoints.code: VII.M.3. Lower leg, medial – Guangming zone
acupoints.name: Guangming
acupoints.anatomy: Saphenous nerve, ocular nerve.
acupoints.location: 1 cun directly behind the tip of the medial malleolus, then 1 cun straight up, at the upper border of the malleolus — that is, 1 cun below Fuliu and 1 cun above Taixi of the fourteen channels.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Liver and Kidney channels.
acupoints.properties: Courses the liver and brightens the eyes.
acupoints.indications: Cataract, sore aching eyes, astigmatism, amblyopia, stroke, hemiplegia.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5 cun; or spot-pricked to bleed with a bloodletting needle.

acupoints.code: VII.A.3. Lower leg, anterior – Shuanglong zone
acupoints.name: Shuanglong yi and Shuanglong er
acupoints.anatomy: Lateral sural cutaneous nerve, branch nerve of the lung, branch nerve of the liver.
acupoints.location: Shuanglong yi is 1.5 cun below the lateral eye of the knee, in the bony depression on the lateral side of the tibia; Shuanglong er is 0.6 cun below it.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Lung and Liver channels.
acupoints.properties: Disperses swelling and relieves pain, courses and frees the channels and connecting vessels.
acupoints.indications: Mastitis, inflammation of the nipple, breast lump, breast cancer.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–0.8 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness, distension, numbness and an electric sensation.
acupoints.application: This point, Jianfeng and Sima all act on the breast, and in practice they are combined to strengthen the effect. Where there is a tumour or cancer, do not forget to add Sanzhong or Waisanguan, the key points for tumours.
acupoints.notes: Shuanglong yi and er are not listed in Master Tung's Orthodox Extraordinary Points of Tung's Acupuncture; they are key points among Tung's 72 principal needlings and were made public by Master Hu in his book. For ordinary breast conditions, first spot-prick to bleed at the heart and lung region of the back (the part of the back corresponding to the breast); and if a bluish vessel shows above the knee, spot-pricking it to release stagnant blood does much to improve breast conditions.

acupoints.code: VIII.A.1. Thigh, anterior – Tonghuo zone
acupoints.name: Tongguan
acupoints.anatomy: Tongguan: femoral nerve, general nerve of the heart. Tongshan: femoral nerve, general nerve of the heart. Tongtian: nerve of the femur, general nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: Tongguan: on the femur along the midline of the thigh, 5 cun above the transverse crease of the knee. Tongshan: on the femur along the midline of the thigh, 2 cun directly above Tongguan. Tongtian: on the femur along the midline of the thigh, 4 cun directly above Tongguan.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Stomach channels.
acupoints.properties: Tongguan: clears the heart and quiets the spirit, loosens the chest and harmonises the stomach. Tongshan: quickens the blood and rectifies qi, calms the heart and quiets the spirit. Tongtian: courses and frees the connecting vessels of the heart, warms the channels and scatters cold.
acupoints.indications: Knee pain, pain in the four limbs, dizziness, blurred vision, cerebral anaemia, stomach conditions, rheumatic heart disease, pain on both sides of the heart, palpitations, heart disease, pain at the heart.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness and distension with slight pain.
acupoints.application: For cardiovascular conditions, bleeding first at responsive areas over the body raises the effect. When Tongxin, Tongling, Tongguan, Tongshan and Tongtian are used as a dao ma or in pairs, Xinling, Huoxing and Linggu may be combined with them.
acupoints.notes: In the Orthodox Extraordinary Points of Tung's Acupuncture, the midline of the upper thigh — the line of Tongxin, Tongguan and Tongshan — belongs to the Heart channel; it is generally used as a three-point dao ma and rarely taken singly. Points in each region of Tung's acupuncture appear in groups of three to five — a defining feature of the system. For conditions of the heart organ itself, treatment in practice requires patience and a long course. Tongxin, Tongling, Tongguan, Tongshan and Tongtian are the five most important points for heart disease; they may also be used for everyday health maintenance and to strengthen circulatory function.

acupoints.name: Tongshan
acupoints.anatomy: Femoral nerve, general nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: On the femur along the midline of the thigh, 2 cun directly above Tongguan.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Stomach channels.
acupoints.properties: Quickens the blood and rectifies qi, calms the heart and quiets the spirit.
acupoints.indications: As for Tongguan.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness and distension with slight pain.
acupoints.notes: In the Orthodox Extraordinary Points of Tung's Acupuncture, the midline of the upper thigh — the line of Tongxin, Tongguan and Tongshan — belongs to the Heart channel; it is generally used as a three-point dao ma and rarely taken singly. Points in each region of Tung's acupuncture appear in groups of three to five — a defining feature of the system.

acupoints.code: VIII.A.1. Thigh, anterior – Tonghuo zone
acupoints.name: Tongxin and Tongling
acupoints.anatomy: Nerve of the femur, general nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: Tongxin lies on the femur along the midline of the leg, 1 cun above the transverse crease of the knee. Tongling is 2 cun directly above Tongxin.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Stomach channels.
acupoints.properties: Calms the heart and quiets the spirit, courses and frees the connecting vessels of the heart.
acupoints.indications: Frontal headache (arising from cardiac enlargement), dizziness, pericardial effusion, restlessness of the heart spirit, chest pain, trembling of the hands and feet, hardening of the vessels, hemiplegia.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–0.8 cun; or oblique insertion from below upward, 0.5–1 cun.
acupoints.notes: Tongxin and Tongling were first made public by Master Hu on the basis of Master Tung's regular teaching, and they are outstandingly effective in treating the circulatory system, the heart and cerebrovascular conditions. The midline on the front of the thigh belongs to the Heart channel among Tung's orthodox extraordinary points, while in the traditional fourteen channels it would fall on the Stomach channel; the author therefore assigns it to both the Heart and Stomach channels. The five points along this line, from above downward, are arranged as a holographic projection of the body's organs — an inverted holographic sequence.

acupoints.name: Tongtian
acupoints.anatomy: Nerve of the femur, general nerve of the heart.
acupoints.location: On the femur along the midline of the thigh, 4 cun directly above Tongguan.
acupoints.meridian: Enters the Heart and Stomach channels.
acupoints.properties: Courses and frees the connecting vessels of the heart, warms the channels and scatters cold.
acupoints.indications: As for Tongguan.
acupoints.technique: Perpendicular insertion, 0.5–1.5 cun.
acupoints.needleFeeling: Soreness and distension with slight pain.
acupoints.application: For cardiovascular conditions, bleeding first at responsive areas over the body raises the effect. When Tongxin, Tongling, Tongguan, Tongshan and Tongtian are used as a dao ma or in pairs, Xinling, Huoxing and Linggu may be combined with them.
